title: Afterlife Contract™
aboutParagraph: Afterlife Contract™ is a conceptual artwork disguised as a legal document. Framed as a luxury "Lifetime Lease + Eternity" agreement from Grim Reaper Inc., it satirizes how humans try to formalise the unformalizable: death, meaning, morality, and hope.
artworkCardDescription: The Underworld isn't a destination, but a curated experience. This original artwork binds cosmic symbols with vintage textures to frame your final choice: three destinations, one signature, and no reliable map. The soul is free; the ink is the only debt.
conceptParagraphs: The project is built around a simple paradox: Everyone gets the afterlife (or non-afterlife) for free—yet humans would still gladly pay for premium access, VIP status, and official confirmation.

This fictional contract echoes reality: the flow is free, but you pay for the package. Energy is abundant, but monetised. Meaning is internal, but outsourced. Freedom exists, yet certificates are sold to validate it.
bureaucracyParagraph: The design borrows the visual language of law and finance—stamps, ledgers, clauses—and applies it to the ultimate unknown. Lines like "Subject to Underworld Adjustments" mock the human desire to regulate what cannot be regulated.
dualityParagraphs: Viewers are invited to "sign" under three deliberately entangled options. Each represents a different existential path: fear/punishment, love/empathy, or creation/meaning-making. Their official names remain filed inside the original contract.
There is no correct answer. The act of choosing (or refusing to choose) becomes the real performance.
visualLanguageParagraph: The work combines holographic gold frames, vintage parchment textures, cartoon skeletons, cosmic symbols, and handwritten annotations—living somewhere between medieval charter, corporate certificate, tarot deck, and internet meme.
filedClausesIntro: Four articles explaining how free eternity acquired premium paperwork.
filedClauseSummaries: Eternity is free. The premium certificate is not.
The unknown has been issued a stamp and several unnecessary clauses.
Three destinations remain entangled until you inspect the evidence.
Part medieval charter, part tarot deck, part internet afterthought.
interactionIntro: The Afterlife Contract is participatory by nature. Viewers are encouraged to:
interactionItems: Laugh, reflect, or feel mildly uncomfortable
interactionClosing: It does not tell the viewer what to believe—it asks why they believe.
closingQuoteLines: The only thing you actually sign
